name: Calculator
description: This project develops a smartphone app for a simple calculator. In its initial version, it allows the user to do basic calculations. More complex calculations will be considered in subsequent versions that are added iteratively.
rawDescription: This project develops a smartphone app for a simple calculator. In its initial version, it allows the user to do basic calculations. More complex calculations will be considered in subsequent versions that are added iteratively.
highLevelGoals: The system shall provide an intuitive and responsive interface that allows the user to perform basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) efficiently and with minimal cognitive load.
The system shall gracefully handle invalid inputs or operational errors (e.g., division by zero) by providing clear, non-technical feedback to the user without crashing or freezing.
The system shall be architected to support the iterative addition of complex calculation features in future versions without requiring significant rework of the core basic calculation logic.
The system shall allow the user to save and review a history of past calculations to facilitate reference and reuse of previous results.
lowLevelGoals: The system shall accept a numeric string input from the user and update the current operand display in the UI.
The system shall accept an arithmetic operator symbol (+, -, *, /) from the user and store it as the pending operation.
The system shall execute the pending arithmetic operation on the stored operands and return the computed result to the display.
The system shall clear the current operand, operator, and result state to prepare for a new calculation sequence.
The system shall validate the input operand against a numeric format schema and reject non-numeric characters.
The system shall detect if the divisor operand is zero before executing a division operation.
The system shall generate a specific error message string for invalid input or division by zero scenarios.
The system shall display the generated error message in the UI and prevent the calculation from completing.
The system shall register a new calculation operation type in the internal operation registry to enable future feature addition.
The system shall map a new UI button or input trigger to a registered calculation operation handler.
The system shall serialize the completed calculation record (operands, operator, result, timestamp) into a persistent storage format.
The system shall write the serialized calculation record to the local device storage or database.
The system shall query the local storage for the list of saved calculation records ordered by timestamp.
The system shall render the retrieved calculation history records in a scrollable list view within the UI.
The system shall load the operands and operator from a selected history record into the active calculation state.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actor "User" is correctly identified as the primary end user of the calculator app. However, there may be additional actors that should be considered for future iterations or maintenance, such as a "Developer" (for updating the app with more complex calculations) and possibly an "Administrator" (if the app requires system-level management in later versions). While the current scope is limited to basic calculations, these roles could be relevant if the project evolves.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined and align with the software description. They cover intuitive basic calculation experience, error handling, future extensibility for complex calculations, and persistence of calculation history. No contradictions or omissions are observed.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and the software description. They cover all necessary functional aspects for a basic calculator app, including input handling, error management, future extensibility, and history persistence. No contradictions or omissions were found.
